html:
Tacitus was a Roman senator and historian, born around 56 CE, whose books are the main source for the early Roman emperors. He is often counted the greatest of Roman historians, known for a dense, sharp style and a dark view of power.

He rose through the offices of state under the Flavian emperors, served as consul in 97 and later governed the province of Asia. His works:

  • Agricola (98), a life of his father-in-law, the general who governed Roman Britain. In it a British chief says of the Romans: "they make a desert and call it peace".
  • Germania (98), on the peoples beyond the Rhine and Danube, the earliest detailed account of them.
  • Histories, covering 69 to 96, beginning with the Year of the Four Emperors.
  • Annals, covering the emperors from Tiberius to Nero, 14 to 68.

The Annals describe the Great Fire of Rome in 64 and Nero's punishment of the Christians. Tacitus adds that their founder, Christus, had been executed under Pontius Pilate, one of the earliest non-Christian mentions of the crucifixion of Jesus.

His friend Pliny the Younger wrote him two letters on the death of his uncle Pliny the Elder in the eruption of Vesuvius. Tacitus died around 120. His books nearly vanished in the Middle Ages and survive in only a few manuscripts.
